page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-64xCPU-384GB is a Cloud Native family server running on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor with 64 vCPUs and 64 physical cores. The CPU operates at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz with a shared allocation model and 1.0 thread per core. The system is equipped with 384.0 GB of system memory, providing 6.0 GB of RAM per core. No local storage or GPU hardware is bundled with this instance type, though it includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data reveals a clear tradeoff between single-core and multi-core performance. The single-core stress-ng CPU performance falls into the bottom 10%, and single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression are weak, placing in the bottom 25%. However, multi-threaded capabilities are significantly stronger, with bzip3 multi-threaded decompression and Passmark CPU scores, including physics, encryption, and extended instructions, ranking in the top 25%. Memory bandwidth is also a notable strength, with read-only small block and write large block tests both scoring in the top 25%.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the shared CPU allocation model and high resource density offer a budget-friendly profile for highly parallelized workloads that do not require dedicated CPU cores. The server is configured for multi-threaded processing tasks, software compilation, database operations, and static web serving. It is less optimal for single-threaded applications or workloads requiring high-speed text processing and real-time large-model LLM text generation, where performance is constrained.
